families.name: Market intraday momentum into the close (rest-of-day or first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour)

mechanism.whose_flow: Gamma hedgers: option market makers short gamma and leveraged-ETF rebalancing trade in the direction of the day's move before the close (Baltussen et al. 2021); late-informed traders (Gao et al. 2018).
mechanism.why_predictable: The hedge size is set mechanically by the day's return and is executed near the close, a known time.
mechanism.why_retail_edge_could_exist: The flow is non-informational and large against a one-lot; the open issue is size per trade against cost (R1-14: NQ T1 gross 1.25 ticks against 4.08 cost).
mechanism.quote: Hedging short gamma exposure requires trading in the direction of price movements, thereby creating price momentum.

families.name: Energy inventory release drift or reversal (EIA WPSR for crude, EIA WNGSR for natural gas, API)

mechanism.why_predictable: Fixed release time (WPSR Wednesday 10:30 ET, CRUDE-13; WNGSR Thursday 10:30 ET, NATGAS-24; API Tuesday 16:30 ET, CRUDE-15).
mechanism.why_retail_edge_could_exist: Only if the post-release path keeps moving or reverses on a scale of 15 minutes to hours; the first minutes belong to fast traders (NATGAS-27: within 50 ms).

families.name: Cross-market lead-lag and relative-value reversion (crush, calendars, mini/micro-full pairs, equity-index lead-lag, gold-silver, AUD-commodities, BTC-ETH)

mechanism.whose_flow: Hedgers and spread traders anchoring an economic relation (crush margin); information arriving first in the deeper market and propagating.
mechanism.why_predictable: Cointegrated legs revert; a leader's move precedes a laggard's.
mechanism.why_retail_edge_could_exist: Only where the lag or the reversion lasts minutes to hours: seconds-scale lead-lag cannot pay at retail latency (E.32 verdict table, M2 b).
